prs.title: fix(shared): preserve MCPError payload on pickle
prs.author: MukundaKatta
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both PRs fix the same underlying bug: MCPError (and its subclass UrlElicitationRequiredError) is not pickle-safe. The default Exception.__reduce_ex__ reconstructs via cls(*self.args), but self.args is set to (code, message, data) by MCPError.__init__ while subclass constructors like UrlElicitationRequiredError's (elicitations, message=None) don't match that signature - causing a TypeError on unpickle and/or loss of the ErrorData payload (referenced by issue #2431). (2 PRs)

prs.title: fix: buffer stdio server writes during progress notifications
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: The stdio server's write_stream memory-object stream is created with buffer_size=0 (a rendezvous/unbuffered channel), forcing stdout_writer to be actively receiving before any sender can complete. This causes a handler trying to send its final JSON-RPC response to block if stdout_writer is still busy flushing an earlier message (e.g. a progress notification), since there's no queue slack. Both PRs touch the exact same line (`write_stream, write_stream_reader = create_context_streams[SessionMessage](0)`) to relieve this blocking. (2 PRs)

prs.title: Fix pre_parse_json corrupting str | None values that look like JSON
prs.author: vientooscuro
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: pre_parse_json() in func_metadata.py calls json.loads() on any string argument whose field annotation isn't exactly `str`, including unions like `str | None`. This corrupts valid string values that happen to look like JSON (e.g. "123", "true", "[1,2]") when the field is typed as an Optional[str]/str-union, since the string gets silently decoded into a different type before validation. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: pre_parse_json() in func_metadata.py calls json.loads() on any string argument whose field annotation isn't exactly `str`, including unions like `str | None`. This corrupts valid string values that happen to look like JSON (e.g. "123", "true", "[1,2]") when the field is typed as an Optional[str]/str-union, since the string gets silently decoded into a different type before validation. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: Both add a helper to gate pre-parsing for union annotations containing str, but the scope of the skip condition differs. #2032's _should_pre_parse_json treats str, int, float, bool, and NoneType as interchangeable '_SIMPLE_TYPES' and skips parsing whenever all union members fall in that set — so it also disables pre-parsing for `str | int`, `str | bool`, and `str | float` fields, not just `str | None`. That changes behavior for numeric-string coercion cases (e.g. a `str | int` field receiving "123" would previously become the int 123 via JSON pre-parse; under #2032 it stays the literal string "123"). #3056's _is_optional_str only matches unions whose non-None members are exactly [str] (i.e. true Optional[str]), leaving pre-parsing behavior for `str | int`/`str | float`/`str | bool` unions untouched, and its diff includes a docstring explaining exactly why only the str-or-None case is safe to skip. The narrower, documented condition in #3056 fixes the reported corruption bug without altering coercion behavior for other str-unions, so it's the safer of the two to keep.

clusters.pick_reason: Both add a helper to gate pre-parsing for union annotations containing str, but the scope of the skip condition differs. #2032's _should_pre_parse_json treats str, int, float, bool, and NoneType as interchangeable '_SIMPLE_TYPES' and skips parsing whenever all union members fall in that set — so it also disables pre-parsing for `str | int`, `str | bool`, and `str | float` fields, not just `str | None`. That changes behavior for numeric-string coercion cases (e.g. a `str | int` field receiving "123" would previously become the int 123 via JSON pre-parse; under #2032 it stays the literal string "123"). #3056's _is_optional_str only matches unions whose non-None members are exactly [str] (i.e. true Optional[str]), leaving pre-parsing behavior for `str | int`/`str | float`/`str | bool` unions untouched, and its diff includes a docstring explaining exactly why only the str-or-None case is safe to skip. The narrower, documented condition in #3056 fixes the reported corruption bug without altering coercion behavior for other str-unions, so it's the safer of the two to keep.

clusters.pick_reason: Both add a helper to gate pre-parsing for union annotations containing str, but the scope of the skip condition differs. #2032's _should_pre_parse_json treats str, int, float, bool, and NoneType as interchangeable '_SIMPLE_TYPES' and skips parsing whenever all union members fall in that set — so it also disables pre-parsing for `str | int`, `str | bool`, and `str | float` fields, not just `str | None`. That changes behavior for numeric-string coercion cases (e.g. a `str | int` field receiving "123" would previously become the int 123 via JSON pre-parse; under #2032 it stays the literal string "123"). #3056's _is_optional_str only matches unions whose non-None members are exactly [str] (i.e. true Optional[str]), leaving pre-parsing behavior for `str | int`/`str | float`/`str | bool` unions untouched, and its diff includes a docstring explaining exactly why only the str-or-None case is safe to skip. The narrower, documented condition in #3056 fixes the reported corruption bug without altering coercion behavior for other str-unions, so it's the safer of the two to keep.

members.title: fix: don't send a response for cancelled requests
members.author: Zelys-DFKH
members.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both PRs rewrite the same code path in RequestResponder.cancel() (src/mcp/shared/session.py) that decides what gets sent back when a request is cancelled. The prior code sent an error response from cancel() and had server.py's _handle_request treat a second response as a 'duplicate' to suppress. #2493 removes the error-response send entirely (cancel() sends nothing, matching the spec text that receivers must not respond to a cancelled request) and updates the server.py comment/log accordingly. #2514 touches the same cancel() method body (dedenting the _entered guard, adding a CancelledNotificationParams import) to instead have cancel() emit a notifications/cancelled message. Both are direct edits to the same lines deciding cancel()'s outbound message, so they will conflict on merge and are fixing the same defect (cancel() sends the wrong thing on cancellation). (2 PRs)
